title: March Leaves Like a Lamb
skyStory: The waning moon, thirty-five percent lit, sits quietly in Capricorn for the last night of March. The month came in like a lion and is leaving like a very sleepy lamb, curled up in a patch of new grass. Saturn tucks a blanket over it. Mars, for once, is quiet. The equinox has passed, the birthday is done, and April is waiting at the door, holding flowers.

reading: Last day of the month: time to look back at the new moon intention you hid inside a book on the sixth. Find it. Read it. You may be surprised. The Tiger carried that one log further than you thought.

Whatever happened with it, celebrate the attempt. The [[Knight of Wands]] did not win every race, but he rode every one with his whole heart. Write a new single sentence for April and tuck it back into the same book. Then close the book, close March, and walk outside to smell the mud. Spring is here. You helped bring it.
joel.mission: Find the intention you hid on March 6, read it aloud, then write a fresh one for April in the same book.
joel.omen: A lamb, sheep or anything woolly and calm. It means the month ended gently, and April will start well.
joel.stoneWhy: stack March on top of April

reading: The last night of March, and the moon is in your sign, keeping you company as the month closes. Look back at the tiny map you drew under the new moon, two dots: where you were, where you were heading. You moved. You definitely moved.

Draw a new map for April. Same rules: two dots, one line between. The [[Six of Swords]] is still mid-crossing, but the water is open now, the ice is gone, the robins are back. The rowing feels lighter. Joel is still rowing beside you. Put the map somewhere secret, and let April surprise you.
nancy.mission: Draw April's tiny map, two dots and one line, and tuck it next to March's map in your secret spot.
nancy.omen: Wind blowing gently from the south. It means the next month brings warmer things, and you are ready for them.

together.text: End-of-March crossing. Each of you send the other one word that sums up this month, and one word for what you want April to be. No explanations. Just two words each, like stepping stones over the creek.

game.intro: March is leaving like a lamb. Catch it on the way out, close enough to see the wool.
game.prompt: Something that changed this month: a melting icicle, a new sprout, a shrinking snowbank. Zoom way in.
